title: 2018_PMC6190029_A_rapid_qualitative_assessment_of_oral_cholera_vaccine_anticipat
ehr_evidence: Questionnaires, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions, as well as observations, were conducted before the campaign.
summary: A rapid qualitative anthropological assessment with quantitative questionnaire data of anticipated acceptability of the oral cholera vaccine in Nampula, Mozambique, involving 143 government informants, community leaders, health workers, and community members.
key_findings: 95% of participants reported knowledge about what cholera is and 66% attributed its principal cause to 'dirtiness' (dirty water 57%, dirty food 39%).
26% of respondents reported previous negative experiences associated with immunization, mainly minor adverse events.
55% of participants preferred injectable vaccine and 40% preferred oral delivery.
Willingness to be vaccinated was very high (95%), driven by high perceived vulnerability and severity of cholera.
83% preferred vaccine administration by health professionals versus 11% by community health workers, and 75% favored public health center-based delivery versus 6% home-based delivery.
captured_features: preferred vaccine delivery route (oral vs injectable)
preferred administrator (health professional vs community worker)
study_design: rapid qualitative assessment (formative anthropological study) with complementary quantitative questionnaire data
population: 143 participants (government informants, community leaders, health workers, community health volunteers, and community members with cholera experience) in three cholera-affected neighborhoods of Nampula City, Mozambique
exposure_domain: oral cholera vaccine acceptability and social/political determinants of vaccine hesitancy
limitations: Purposive, convenience, and chain-referral sampling was used, so findings are not representative and cannot be generalized to a broader population.
Cultural, social, and historical determinants may vary geographically and temporally, limiting applicability to other populations or later time points.
